title: An international comparison: the EU AI Act

sources.claim: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, in force August 1, 2024) uses risk tiers: some practices are prohibited (from February 2, 2025), high-risk systems face requirements, and some systems face transparency duties. A 2026 amendment ("digital omnibus", in force July 27, 2026) moved most Annex III high-risk obligations to December 2, 2027.

sections.skill: Describe the EU AI Act's risk-based approach and dated timeline

questions.prompt: When did the EU AI Act enter into force?
questions.intro: As an international comparison, the European Union's AI ACT (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) entered into force on August 1, 2024. It takes a RISK-BASED approach: some practices are PROHIBITED (applying from February 2, 2025); HIGH-RISK systems, such as some used in hiring, education or credit, face requirements like risk management and human oversight; some systems face TRANSPARENCY duties, such as telling people they are interacting with AI. A 2026 amendment, in force July 27, 2026, moved most high-risk obligations for systems listed in its Annex III to December 2, 2027.

questions.prompt: What kind of approach does the Act take?

sections.skill: Compare risk tiers with rules for vehicles

questions.prompt: Driving with no brakes is like which tier?

choices.text: High-risk, which means it is allowed with extra training and regular safety inspections

questions.intro: Rules for vehicles depend on RISK: a bicycle needs few rules, a car needs a license and insurance, a large truck carrying hazardous materials needs special training and inspections, and some things, like driving with no brakes, are simply banned. The EU AI Act uses similar tiers: some practices banned, high-risk systems heavily regulated, some systems with transparency duties, and many with few specific rules.

questions.prompt: Why does the course set a short review interval for the EU AI Act?

choices.text: Because the Act is expected to be cancelled completely within the next few weeks

questions.intro: Timelines like these change, which is why the course dates every claim and sets a short review interval for this one. The Act applies in the EU, but can affect companies elsewhere that offer AI systems there. Comparing approaches helps: the EU has one broad regulation, while the US mostly relies on existing laws, agency actions and state laws. Neither approach is presented here as right; each reflects different choices and trade-offs.
